newsitem.title: USA: Sumitomo Trust unit orders 4 Boeing jets. [CORRECTED 19:25 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Sumitomo Trust unit orders 4 Boeing jets. [CORRECTED 19:25 GMT]

text.p: Boullioun Aviation Services, a leasing company owned by Sumitomo Trust & Banking Co Ltd, has ordered four Boeing Co 737-300 jets valued at about $140 million, an executive said Friday.

Bob Penski (corrects first name from Jim), executive vice president of the Bellevue, Wash.-based leasing company, said the planes are scheduled for delivery in 1998 and come on top of a previously announced order for eight 737-300s for delivery in 1997 and 1998.
Boullioun currently owns about 20 jets, mostly Boeing narrow-bodied 737s and 757s that are leased to airlines around the world.
Boullioun was founded a decade ago by legendary Boeing salesman "Tex" Boullioun and was bought by Sumitomo about 18 months ago, Penski said.
The company now employs about 40 people including satellite offices in London and Singapore.
Penski said that with the jets on order he believes Boullioun ranks as the world's third biggest jet leasing company.
